title: Evaluate a reverse-polish expression
prompt:
Write evaluateRPN(String[] tokens) returning the int value of the reverse-polish
expression in tokens. Every token is either an integer literal (possibly negative) or
one of the operators "+", "-", "*", "/". The expression is always valid and holds at
least one token, so a lone operand evaluates to itself, and no division by zero occurs.

Operands are consumed in the order they were pushed: for tokens [a, b, "-"] the answer
is a - b, and for [a, b, "/"] it is a / b. Division is integer division that truncates
toward zero, so -7 / 2 is -3, not -4.

Examples:
  evaluateRPN(["2", "1", "+", "3", "*"]) -> 9
  evaluateRPN(["4", "13", "5", "/", "+"]) -> 6
  evaluateRPN(["5"])                      -> 5

Keep the class name Solution and the given method signature.
